A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FairDD research, with matching authors, core objective, theory, and experiments. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original dataset-distillation experiments measuring fairness and accuracy, cross-architecture evaluations, computational costs, and numerous appendix ablations.

after.justification: V2 retains original experimental results and adds benchmark evaluations, fairness-specific comparisons, and experiments with missing protected attributes and pseudo-group labels.

M1.justification: The core synchronized group-matching objective remains unchanged. V2 Appendix M adds an implemented adaptation using batchwise DBSCAN clustering to supply pseudo-group labels when protected-attribute labels are unavailable; v1 only suggested unsupervised pseudo-labeling as future work.

E1.justification: V2 adds BFFHQ, six biased ImageNet subsets, and Tiny-ImageNet-S, while removing the CIFAR100-S evaluation. UTKFace is retained but its protected attribute changes from gender in v1 Appendix D to race in v2 Table 8. Missing training group labels and absent protected-attribute groups at test time introduce additional input and test scenarios.

E2.justification: V2 adds evaluated comparisons with DM+LW, DM+LfF, DC+MF, DC+DF, and Cui et al. (2024), plus LDAM and GroupDRO weighting variants. V1's FairDDinverse corresponds to FairDD+IW, rather than a new comparator; the plain DM comparator is removed from that weighting comparison. The principal DM, DC, IDC, DREAM, and MTT comparisons remain.

E3.justification: The reported initialization comparison changes from random/noise/hybrid to proportion/balanced initialization at IPC=50. The weighting study expands from IPC=10 to IPC=10 and 50, and new controls alter extractor training or the stage of fairness intervention. New testing procedures remove one, two, or three protected-attribute groups while retaining all groups during training. The principal metrics and default bias ratio remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds analyses testing fair extractors, fairness interventions during distillation versus classifier training, absent test groups, and DBSCAN pseudo-labels. It expands weighting ablations and replaces noise/hybrid initialization results with balanced initialization. Existing noisy-label, balanced-data, intersecting-attribute, minority-imbalance, and ViT analyses are largely retained under different appendix labels.

E5.justification: V1 Appendix O, Tables 21–25, reports means and standard deviations for main comparisons, cross-architecture evaluations, and ablations. V2 removes these uncertainty tables and reports point estimates, while newly stating in checklist item 7 that results average five runs. This changes statistical reporting substantially without establishing an increase in run counts.

E6.justification: The original six datasets' main-table means are retained, but v2 adds extensive benchmark, comparator, and ablation results and removes CIFAR100-S and noise/hybrid initialization entries. UTKFace results are replaced under a different protected-attribute setting. Some reused values also change inconsistently: C-FMNIST (BG) FairDD DEOM at IPC=10 changes from 33.05 in v1 Table 12 to 26.87 in v2 Table 10, although v2 Table 1 retains 33.05.

T1.justification: V2 Appendix J adds a computational-complexity argument comparing groupwise G·O(m/G)+O(n) processing with O(m)+O(n). The principal fairness and coverage theorems remain substantively unchanged; their compressed notation and relocation of the coverage proof to Appendix D do not constitute new theoretical results.

C1.justification: The abstract qualifies v1's claim of improving fairness 'without sacrificing classification accuracy' as a 'promising trade-off between fairness and accuracy.' V2 also explicitly frames the contribution as data-level fairness. The central claims concerning synchronized matching, bias mitigation, and applicability across matching-based distillation methods remain.

C2.justification: V2 substantially expands explanations of why fair extractors, stage-specific fairness interventions, density weighting, and worst-group alignment can remain inadequate. It adds interpretations of missing test groups and pseudo-label applicability, and revises the computational-overhead explanation around GPU parallelism. The original limitation concerning dependence on protected-attribute information remains, despite the new exploratory workaround.

D1.justification: V2 adds a code-repository link, UTKFace/BFFHQ dataset statistics, and procedural descriptions for DBSCAN and additional weighting controls. The PyTorch version and GPU specification remain unchanged. The abstract's code-availability statement conflicts with the checklist's promise of a future release, so actual availability is not established by the PDFs.

R1.justification: Section 2 and Appendix E substantially expand positioning against Cui et al.'s bias-mitigation approach, asserting differences in protected-group coverage, information preservation, and theoretical support. V2 sharpens the distinction from model-level fairness and fairness-aware generation, and adds distinct references including Learning from Failure, GroupDRO, and GIFT. Duplicate or updated references are not separate additions.

P1.justification: V2 shortens the title, moves related work before the preliminaries, and relocates dataset descriptions, the coverage proof, representation-coverage analysis, and bias-ratio ablations into reorganized appendices. It adds an appendix guide and conference checklist and substantially expands the discussion and related-work narrative.

P2.justification: Figure 1 recombines existing visualizations and the fairness chart, while Figure 2 replaces the detailed illustrated pipeline with a compact schematic. Main tables expand and are packed into a different layout; several new tables appear, and the standard-deviation tables disappear. Existing feature plots and appendix image grids are largely retained or relocated, with some caption corrections.

improvement.justification: New fairness-specific controls, broader benchmark coverage, and missing-label experiments strengthen the evaluation. However, v2 removes v1's standard-deviation reporting and introduces conflicting comparison values in Tables 10 and 18; for example, Table 18 reports IPC=10 prior-label accuracy of 96.86 where Table 2 reports 94.88. These gains coexist with reduced statistical transparency and unresolved numerical inconsistencies, preventing a reliable net-quality judgment.
